anatomy.detail: Drawing number, revision letter (A, B, C...), date, drawn-by, checked-by, scale, material specification, weight. ALWAYS check revision letter — old prints have killed parts.

anatomy.part: Revision block (upper right or in title block)
anatomy.detail: Lists each revision with date + description + initials. Compare to your drawing — if the part you're holding doesn't match the print revision, STOP.
Lists every part by number + quantity + material spec. Cross-reference part labels in the drawing.
Standard arrangement: top view above front view, right side view to the right of front view. Third-angle projection (US standard) vs first-angle (European) — verify symbol in title block.
Cutaway showing internal features. Section line on parent view, "A-A" or "B-B" labels identify which cutting plane.
In inches (or mm for international). Dimensions to important features, not to arbitrary points. "TYP" or "TYPICAL" = applies to multiple similar features.
Default tolerances stated near title block (e.g., "X.XX = ±0.030 unless noted"). Specific tolerances override defaults.
Per AWS A2.4. Symbol direction matters — see Symbols module. Multiple welds get multiple symbols.
GENERAL NOTES near title block apply to whole drawing. LOCAL notes near specific features apply only there. Read them ALL before starting.

checklist: 1. ✓ Revision letter matches BOM + work order
2. ✓ Material spec matches stock you're cutting from
5. ✓ Weld symbols clear (process, size, length, location)
6. ✓ Cut + drill operations sequenced (some must precede others)
intro: Most welding mistakes are misread prints, not bad welding. Knowing the conventions saves time + scrap.
crosslink: Try it on a real layout: the Symbols Reader has a three-view bracket drawing with four symbols to read.
